newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia coffee harvest seen starting 1 month late.
newsitem.headline: Colombia coffee harvest seen starting 1 month late.

text.p: Colombia's main coffee harvest could begin one month late because of heavy rains during the flowering period earlier this year, a coffee expert said Tuesday.

"Our registers show the flowering period was about one month late. We think, therefore, that the harvest can be expected to be about one month late," Orlando Guzman, an agroclimatologist at the CENICAFE research center, told Reuters.
CENICAFE, based in central Caldas province, is funded by the National Coffee Growers' Federation.
Instead of starting in September, the main harvest, which provides about 60 percent of the country's crop, may not get underway until October, according to Guzman.
That would mean the peak of the harvest would not come until November or December, Guzman said.

He added, however, that the El Nino effect, which has brought exceptionally hot, dry spells to Colombia's main coffee-growing region, could compensate for the wet weather in February and March, thereby partially offsetting delays in the harvest.
Colombia's 1996/97 harvest seems set to come in at just below 10 million 60-kg bags. The forecast for the 1997/98 cycle is for about 12 million bags, according to federation sources.
